subject: Artificial Intelligence
title: Artificial Intelligence — Class 10 (2024)
instructions: 21 questions in two sections; candidates answer 15 in 2 hours for 50 marks. Section A: objective blocks Q1-Q5 (24 marks, internal 'answer any N of M' choice inside each block). Section B: subjective - Q6-Q10 employability (any 3 of 5, 2 marks), Q11-Q16 (any 4 of 6, 2 marks), Q17-Q21 (any 3 of 5, 4 marks). Word limits as printed.

questions.question_text: Objective block (answer any 4 of 6 one-mark parts on Employability Skills): (i) communication - receiver decodes and gives ________ (feedback); (ii) kind of motivation with no apparent reward (intrinsic/extrinsic/...); (iii) personality disorder of one who trusts no one and holds grudges; (iv) how to protect a spreadsheet from being opened or edited on a shared laptop; (v) which is NOT an environmental barrier for an entrepreneur; (vi) which is not a greenhouse gas.

criteria.description: Correct answer for each attempted part, 1 mark each for any four parts

questions.question_text: Objective block (answer any 5 of 6 one-mark parts): (i) statements on capstone projects (final project; independent research) - evaluate; (ii) three key elements of data storytelling; (iii) which statement about RMSE is true; (iv) which is NOT one of the three main stages of an AI project life-cycle; (v) first step of the six-step AI project process; (vi) which statement about the design/build stage is true.

criteria.description: Correct answer for each attempted part, 1 mark each for any five parts

questions.question_text: Objective block (answer any 5 of 6 one-mark parts): (i) which is NOT one of the six steps in an AI project; (ii) why narrative matters in data storytelling; (iii) meaning of 'garbage in, garbage out' for an AI project; (iv) a long-term benefit of data storytelling; (v) primary focus of design thinking; (vi) which is NOT a key activity of the scoping phase of an AI model life-cycle.

criteria.description: Correct answer for each attempted part, 1 mark each for any five parts

questions.question_text: Objective block (answer any 5 of 6 one-mark parts): (i) the AI project cycle stage covering planning and motivational aspects; (ii) structured approach for communicating insights with visuals and narratives; (iii) a good model's RMSE should be less than ________; (iv) the narrative is accompanied with ________ to explain why an insight was generated; (v) which is not an AI development platform; (vi) assertion-reason on MSE as a regression loss function.

criteria.description: Correct answer for each attempted part, 1 mark each for any five parts

questions.question_text: Objective block (answer any 5 of 6 one-mark parts): (i) match icons to data / visuals / narrative; (ii) true or false - if there is no pattern in the data, AI development techniques may be employed; (iii) which is NOT an open framework used in AI model building; (iv) first and last stages of the 5-stage design-thinking process; (v) true or false - human biases in selecting test data can adversely impact testing; (vi) which analytical approach should be used to show relationships.

criteria.description: Correct answer for each attempted part, 1 mark each for any five parts

questions.question_text: There are five stages of active listening; the first is 'Receiving'. Write the names of the other four stages. (20-30 words; part of 'answer any 3 of 5' Employability Skills set)

criteria.description: Any four correct remaining stages named (understanding, evaluating, remembering, responding), half mark each

questions.question_text: Explain the term 'personality traits'. Name any two parameters that describe a personality based on the Five Factor Model. (20-30 words)

criteria.description: Correct explanation of personality traits (enduring characteristics/patterns of thinking, feeling, behaving)
Any two Five-Factor parameters named (openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, neuroticism), half mark each

questions.question_text: Write the steps to print a presentation. (20-30 words)

criteria.description: Correct opening of the print command (File menu > Print / Ctrl+P)
Correct completion (select printer, slides/copies and settings, then Print/OK)

questions.question_text: List any four qualities of a successful entrepreneur. (20-30 words)

criteria.description: Any four valid qualities listed, half mark each

questions.question_text: Write any two ways to minimise waste and pollution in manufacturing plants and factories. (20-30 words)

criteria.description: Two valid ways stated, 1 mark each

questions.question_text: Briefly explain the cross-validation procedure used to validate a model. (20-30 words; part of 'answer any 4 of 6' set)

criteria.description: Core idea correct (splitting data into folds/subsets, training and validating on rotating folds)
Purpose or completion correct (each fold serves as validation once; results averaged for a robust estimate)

questions.question_text: What is train-test split evaluation? For which two types of problems can it be used? (20-30 words)

criteria.description: Correct meaning (dataset divided into a training set and a held-back testing set to evaluate the model)
The two problem types named (classification and regression), half mark each

questions.question_text: Write any two factors that make storytelling a powerful and integral part of indigenous culture. (20-30 words)

criteria.description: Two valid factors stated (e.g. passing knowledge across generations, memorability, emotional connection, shared identity), 1 mark each

questions.question_text: Draw a diagram to represent the foundational methodology for data science. (20-30 words)

criteria.description: Key stages of the methodology present (from business understanding through data preparation, modelling, evaluation, deployment, feedback)
Cyclic/ordered flow shown correctly

questions.question_text: 'Time series decomposition involves thinking of a series as a combination of level, trend, seasonality and noise components.' Define any two of these components. (20-30 words)

criteria.description: First chosen component correctly defined
Second chosen component correctly defined

questions.question_text: With respect to evaluation of AI development platforms, give any two examples each of (a) open languages, (b) productivity-enhancing capabilities. (20-30 words)

criteria.description: Two valid open languages (e.g. Python, R, Scala), half mark each
Two valid productivity-enhancing capabilities (e.g. visual modelling/drag-and-drop tools, AutoML, notebooks, pre-built model APIs), half mark each

questions.question_text: List the steps that can assist in finding compelling stories in data sets. (50-80 words; part of 'answer any 3 of 5' set)

criteria.description: Any four valid steps listed and in a sensible order (e.g. get the data and think of analysis, understand context/audience, explore visualisations, find and refine the insight/story), 1 mark each

questions.question_text: (a) What is a loss function? Write the two categories of loss functions. (b) Explain, with an example, when to use MSE as the loss function. (50-80 words)

criteria.description: Loss function correctly defined (measures how far predictions deviate from actual values)
Two categories written (regression losses and classification losses)
When to use MSE explained (regression targets, normally distributed around a mean, penalises large errors)
A suitable example given (e.g. predicting house prices/temperature)

questions.question_text: Explain the following stages of every AI project life-cycle: (a) requirements analysis, (b) building the model. (50-80 words)

criteria.description: Requirements analysis explained (understanding the problem, planning, feasibility, stakeholder needs)
Building the model explained (selecting/constructing algorithms, training with prepared data, iterating)

questions.question_text: 'Picking an analytic approach to solve a problem is based on the type of question.' Explain the statement with suitable examples. (50-80 words)

criteria.description: Explains the link between question type and approach (descriptive for current status, diagnostic for why, predictive for what will happen, prescriptive/classification for what to do, statistical for relationships)
At least two suitable question-to-approach examples given

questions.question_text: (a) How do good stories emerge? (b) Given two rank charts of states comparing least forest area lost with maximum GSDP growth (2001-22) - one unlabelled, one with a legend - state which is the better data story and give reasons. (50-80 words)

criteria.description: How good stories emerge explained (exploring/questioning the data, context and audience, insights surfacing through visual exploration)
Better chart identified (the labelled/legended one) with valid reasons (legend and labels supply context, make the comparison interpretable)
